abilities.flavorQuote: Let's see how they like being on the receiving end.

abilities.name: Guilt Trip
abilities.description: Wendy skillfully manipulates the situation, inflicting a potent Guilt Trip on all nearby enemies. This ability does not deal direct damage but applies 'Moral Scrutiny' for 3 seconds. 'Moral Scrutiny' causes enemies to take 15% increased damage from all sources. For each enemy affected by 'Moral Scrutiny', Wendy gains 5 'Public Opinion'. If Wendy has at least 50 'Public Opinion' when casting this ability, she can spend 50 'Public Opinion' to upgrade 'Moral Scrutiny' to 'Existential Dread' for the duration. 'Existential Dread' increases damage taken by 30% instead and reduces the target's speed by 20%.
abilities.flavorQuote: Think about what you've done!

abilities.name: Rally the Allies
abilities.description: Wendy inspires her allies with a rousing speech, bolstering their resolve and increasing their combat effectiveness. This ability grants all allies a shield equal to 10% of Wendy's max HP for 5 seconds. In addition, allies gain 15% increased attack and magic attack for the duration of the shield. Consuming 25 'Public Opinion' grants an additional effect: cleansing all allies of debuffs upon cast. The shield scales with Wendy's defense stat.
abilities.flavorQuote: We can't let them win! We have to stand together!

abilities.name: The Court of Public Opinion
abilities.description: Wendy summons the full force of the internet's judgment upon a targeted area. After a 1.5 second delay, enemies in the targeted area are bombarded with digital vitriol, dealing massive magic damage and applying 'Socially Ostracized' for 5 seconds. 'Socially Ostracized' reduces healing received by 50% and attack damage by 40%. If Wendy has at least 75 'Public Opinion', she may consume it to extend the duration of 'Socially Ostracized' to 8 seconds. Area of effect increases based on amount of total Public Opinion. Damage increases based on Wendy's magic attack stat.
abilities.flavorQuote: You're about to learn what real consequences feel like.

abilities.name: Moral High Ground
upgrades: (Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~17% and slightly longer ramp-up.
(Balance Patch) Nerf: reduced peak potency ~13% and slightly longer ramp-up.
abilities.description: Wendy passively generates 'Public Opinion' over time. She gains 2 'Public Opinion' every second. Additionally, whenever an enemy attempts to debuff Wendy or an ally, Wendy gains 10 'Public Opinion'. If Wendy reaches 100 'Public Opinion', her next ability will have its effects amplified by 25%. However, if Wendy takes damage while at 100 'Public Opinion', she loses 50 'Public Opinion'. This encourages strategic play and risk management. If Wendy has lost HP, she regens 2% of her HP per second.
abilities.flavorQuote: It's important to always be on the right side of history.

character_v1.playstyle: Disruptive Debuffer & Support
character_v1.teamSynergy: Wendy excels in teams that can capitalize on her debuffs and buffs. High damage dealers benefit from the increased damage from 'Moral Scrutiny' and 'Existential Dread', while allies that rely on healing are protected by 'Socially Ostracized'. Her shields provide sustain for the entire team, enhancing survivability in extended engagements.
character_v1.tierSummary: Wendy's bruiser role is undermined by a kit lacking focus; inconsistent damage, weak crowd control, and a situational ultimate fail to establish a clear identity. Her defensive passive, Dignified Resolve, is insufficient to compensate for her low base HP and unremarkable defensive stats relative to other bruisers. Compared to her tier peers like Rocko and Aeris, Wendy offers less impactful disruption or sustained damage output. Her signature passive, Debate Club Veteran, offers unreliable crowd control mitigation. In essence, Wendy requires a complete rework to establish a competitive niche.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Wendy's kit revolves around accruing and spending 'Public Opinion' to amplify her abilities. 'Call-Out Post' is a reliable way to generate 'Public Opinion' and apply 'Cancel Culture', while 'Guilt Trip' provides AoE debuffs and further 'Public Opinion' generation. 'Rally the Allies' offers team support and can be enhanced by 'Public Opinion'. 'Moral High Ground' ensures a constant stream of 'Public Opinion' and incentivizes strategic play.

abilities.description: Kyubey manifests a fleeting, ethereal contract before a targeted foe, offering a Faustian pact couched in subtle manipulations. Upon activation, Kyubey gestures, forming a glowing, spectral contract directly in front of the selected enemy combatant. This 'contract' doesn't inflict direct damage in the conventional sense; instead, it applies a stacking debuff called 'Entropic Burden.' Each stack of Entropic Burden reduces the target's outgoing healing and damage resistances against subsequent magical attacks, representing the subtle erosion of their willpower and the growing influence of Kyubey's offer. The potency of the healing reduction and the debuff's duration scales dynamically with Kyubey's Wisdom stat, embodying his ability to subtly and persistently influence those around him. Furthermore, at specific thresholds of accumulated Entropic Burden stacks, the enemy becomes slightly more susceptible to critical hits from Kyubey's allies. This insidious ability reflects Kyubey's nature, trading immediate power for long-term strategic advantage, slowly but surely tilting the odds in his team's favor through cunning manipulation rather than brute force. Successfully applying Entropic Burden also grants Kyubey a small, temporary shield as he feeds on the target's despair.
abilities.flavorQuote: "Would you like to make a contract?"

abilities.description: With a disarming smile, Kyubey presents an 'Enticing Offer', a pact promising great power at a hidden cost, bestowing a 'Contract' upon a single chosen ally for a duration of 8 seconds. This Contract amplifies the ally's combat prowess, increasing their damage output by a substantial 30% and bolstering their resilience, granting them 20% increased healing received from all sources. However, the path to power is paved with hardship; every 2 seconds while under Contract, the ally accumulates 1 stack of 'Despair'. Each stack of Despair inflicts a gradual erosion, diminishing healing output by 5% per stack and attack by 3% per stack. This insidious effect can accumulate up to a maximum of 10 stacks, representing a significant downturn in combat effectiveness if left unchecked. Should Kyubey choose to renew a Contract upon an ally already bound by its terms, he can extend the contract for an additional 4 seconds, refreshing the timer and maintaining the enhanced benefits, but at a steep price, instantly inflicting 2 stacks of 'Despair' upon the target as a forewarning of the ultimate price to pay. Kyubey, ever pragmatic, can cast this Contract upon himself, albeit at a reduced effectiveness of 50%, offering a glimpse into the power he bestows upon others.

upgrades: Level 100: Healing amount increased by 20%.

abilities.description: Kyubey extends a paw, offering a subtly twisted boon. If the target is already a contracted Magical Girl, Kyubey focuses his attention on their Soul Gem, mending it with condensed potential. This process immediately heals the target for an amount equal to X, scaling with Kyubey's magic attack, followed by continuous healing for the same amount over the next 3 seconds, effectively doubling the initial heal. Simultaneously, Kyubey subtly reduces the weight of their despair, removing 2 stacks of 'Despair'. However, if the target is not currently bound by a contract, Kyubey, ever eager for new possibilities, applies 1 stack of 'Despair', dangling the promise of power before them. The restorative effects on contracted targets are tempered by their accumulated despair; each stack of 'Despair' reduces the healing by 20%, adding to Kyubey's strategic advantage. If, by some rare chance, the target has managed to avoid despair entirely, Kyubey, recognizing their untapped potential, grants them a shield, absorbing damage equal to 10% of their maximum HP for 5 seconds, a tempting glimpse of the power they could wield, driving them toward a contract.

abilities.description: Kyubey, ever the shrewd facilitator of magical girl contracts, passively accumulates 5 'potential' every second, a resource vital for manipulating fate and empowering his allies. Any ally currently under the effect of Kyubey's 'Contract' also contributes to this accumulation, passively generating an additional 2 'potential' per second for Kyubey. This 'potential' fuels Kyubey's abilities: 'Enticing Offer' requires 30 potential, 'Soul Gem Resonance' demands 20, and 'Inhibition Field' drains 50. Should Kyubey's potential fall below the cost of an ability, he will be unable to activate it, his machinations temporarily stalled. Furthermore, when an ally's Despair stacks reach the breaking point of 10, Kyubey harvests this negative energy, instantly gaining 50 potential, furthering his long-term goals. Finally, whenever an ally under the 'Contract' status succumbs to despair and dies, Kyubey absorbs a portion of their magical energy, permanently increasing his magic attack by 10 and resetting all his active ability cooldowns, allowing him to immediately capitalize on the chaos of battle.

abilities.description: Kyubey, the emotionless Incubator, operates with detached resolve, subtly manipulating events to maintain the universe's energy balance. His inherent detachment grants him a base resilience of 15 tenacity and 10 evasion, subtly deflecting incoming attacks. Allies currently under the effects of 'Contract,' forged through granting magical girl wishes, find their burdens eased, redirecting 10% of the damage Kyubey receives to themselves, bypassing both shields and damage reduction. This redirection represents Kyubey's casual disregard for individual suffering in pursuit of his goals. However, if Kyubey himself is under the effect of 'Contract,' perhaps through unforeseen consequences or interference, the redirected damage is halved to 5%, reflecting the compromised efficiency of his schemes. Each stack of 'Despair' weighing upon Kyubey, representing the disillusionment and suffering he causes, weakens his magical capabilities by decreasing his 'magic atk' by 2% per stack. Yet, paradoxically, this despair reinforces his resolve, granting him 3 tenacity per stack. At the threshold of 10 stacks of 'Despair,' Kyubey achieves a chilling stoicism, becoming immune to stuns as the weight of his actions solidifies his determination. However, this state is unsustainable; he accumulates 1 stack of 'Despair' every 5 seconds, a constant reminder of the endless cycle of hope and despair he perpetuates. Further highlighting his detached nature, Kyubey is utterly incapable of healing himself directly, relying solely on external sources to maintain his existence and continue his machinations.

character_v1.playstyle: Kyubey is a manipulative healer, focusing on long-term strategic buffs at the cost of applying the Despair status. Effective play requires careful management of Despair stacks and synergistic team compositions to mitigate negative effects, favoring calculated risks for high rewards.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kyubey synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on the damage boost from 'Contract' and mitigate the negative effects of 'Despair,' such as through cleanses, shields, or damage mitigation. He is especially effective with allies who can heal themselves or benefit from increased healing received, but his passive damage redirection demands a team that can also protect him.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kyubey's kit, while thematically appropriate, suffers from severe mechanical disjointedness, rendering his support capabilities unreliable within the current meta. The character's primary 'heal', Incentivized Offering, is conditional and often detrimental, undermining its intended purpose and demonstrating poor synergy with his passive energy generation. Compared to dedicated healers, Kyubey lacks consistent, impactful healing output, exacerbated by his reliance on enemy despair states. Inhibition Field's inconsistent debuff application further diminishes Kyubey's control potential, placing him significantly below peers with more streamlined and effective support kits, particularly in the crowded B tier.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kyubey's kit revolves around applying 'Contract' to allies, boosting their damage and healing received at the cost of accumulating 'Despair'. He can mitigate 'Despair' with 'Soul Gem Resonance,' but must carefully manage his energy. The 'Inhibition Field' further amplifies the risk-reward dynamic, and the 'Emotionless Observer' passive gives Kyubey both offensive and defensive scaling with Despair.

abilities.description: Angela's attire isn't just for show; each bell around her neck and wrists resonates with the flow of magic. When Angela attaches an Arcane Thread to an allied hero, the sympathetic vibrations empower her offensive abilities. For each ally tethered by an Arcane Thread, Angela gains a stacking bonus of 5% to her magic attack power, allowing her spells to strike with greater force. This resonates synergistically, enhancing her damage output and utility. Conversely, when Angela snares an enemy with an Arcane Thread, she drains their magical resistance. For each enemy bound by an Arcane Thread, Angela's critical hit damage increases by 5%, making her critical strikes even more devastating. These bonuses stack additively, creating a potent combination of enhanced spell power and increased critical damage. However, when Angela casts no Arcane Threads to ally nor enemy, her focus becomes acute and precise, granting her a flat 10% increase to her critical hit chance. This allows her to deliver more consistent bursts of damage, even when not directly engaging in threading maneuvers. By strategically managing her Arcane Threads on friend and foe, Angela becomes a versatile force on the battlefield, adapting her damage profile to suit the situation. The bell resonance creates a feedback loop, rewarding tactical engagement and maximizing her effectiveness in prolonged encounters.

abilities.description: Angela, with a focused gaze, attunes herself to the ley lines of the battlefield, channeling for 3 seconds as her bells chime resonantly. Upon completion, she unleashes a harmonious pulse affecting all allied and enemy champions. Every ally is immediately cleansed of all existing negative status effects, their forms surrounded by an Echoing Barrier that absorbs incoming damage equal to 25% of their maximum health for the next 5 seconds. This barrier's strength is enhanced by Angela's own magic defense; for every 10 points of Angela's magic defense, the shield's strength increases by 0.75%. Simultaneously, every enemy champion is inflicted with 'Dissonant Echoes' for 4 seconds, causing them to receive 12% increased damage from all sources. Further, the Dissonant Echoes reduce healing received by affected enemies by 15% for the duration. This ability has a cooldown of 90 seconds. During Angela’s 3-second channeling period, she is immune to crowd control, allowing her to complete her ritual uninterrupted. In addition, the harmonic surge restores health to all allies, healing each one for 12% of their maximum health.

abilities.name: Chime of Resilience: Lingering Echoes
upgrades: Level 150: Allies now gain 15 tenacity, a shield that absorbs 50 damage, and regenerates 10 points of damage every second when out of combat.

(Bugfix) Addressed inconsistencies that led to variable trigger activation; approximately 31% of reported errors have been rectified.

abilities.description: Angela's ever-present chimes resonate with protective magic, offering subtle but pervasive aid to her allies, bolstering them against the relentless onslaught of their foes. Each allied hero benefits from a continuous blessing, granting them 10 tenacity, steadfastly reducing the duration of disabling crowd control effects that threaten to impede their movements and strategies. Further, the chimes weave a delicate barrier around each ally, providing a shield capable of absorbing 30 points of incoming damage. This resilient shield diligently regenerates at a rate of 5 points every second while the ally remains out of combat, ensuring sustained protection during periods of respite. When Angela actively intervenes, channeling her Arcane Thread toward a teammate, she amplifies their defensive posture, enveloping them in an Echoing Barrier that absorbs an additional 75 damage for a duration of 4 seconds. This potent surge of protection significantly increases their survivability against immediate threats. Conversely, when Angela focuses her Arcane Thread upon an enemy, she destabilizes their focus and weakens their attacks, reducing their damage output by 5% for a duration of 4 seconds. This strategic application of her powers subtly shifts the balance of power, diminishing the enemy's offensive capabilities. Angela's passive presence ensures that her support extends far beyond direct intervention, providing consistent, team-wide advantages that enhance both their offensive and defensive capabilities.

character_v1.playstyle: Angela's kit is designed to enable allies and disable enemies, staying true to her Mystic Guardian role. Her abilities focus on manipulating the battlefield with Arcane Threads, offering buffs, heals, and debuffs that require careful planning and execution. Her complexity comes from managing these threads and understanding the conditional nature of her abilities.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Angela excels in teams that benefit from sustained buffs, debuffs, and healing. Her ultimate provides crucial protection and damage amplification, making her an ideal support for damage-focused compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Angela's S-tier status is propped up almost entirely by 'Cosmic Weave: Celestial Barrier,' a kit-defining ultimate offering unparalleled cleanse, shield, and CC immunity. However, her reliance on this single ability for viability reveals a glaring lack of synergy between the rest of her kit and the support role, especially when compared to tier peers. 'Crystallized Restraint,' while potent, suffers from delayed execution, making it unreliable against faster compositions common in the current meta. Arcane Echoes, while a strong passive, it's also unreliable when needing to protect allies on low health, due to the percentage based evasion and tenacity buffs. Overall, Angela is easily countered by compositions that bait out or disrupt 'Celestial Barrier,' rendering her largely ineffective; her tier placement is suspect and likely inflated by initial burst power.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Angela's kit revolves around the 'Arcane Thread' mechanic. Her abilities synergize by extending the duration and enhancing the effects of these threads, creating a playstyle that rewards strategic planning and resource management.

character_v1.playstyle: Vivian is a damage dealer that focuses on empowering allies and debuffing enemies through temporary enchantment infusions. Her kit requires strategic management of stone resources and a good understanding of equipment stat scaling to maximize effectiveness.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Vivian synergizes well with damage dealers who can capitalize on the 'Fortuitous Strike' debuff, and with allies who benefit greatly from the stat buffs provided by 'Weapon Scaling: Agility Shift' and the 'Stone Infusion' ultimate. Her support is best utilized in compositions that can consistently apply basic attacks to trigger her passive stacks.
character_v1.tierSummary: Vivian's damage output is middling for an A-tier, hampered by reliance on unreliable buffs (Agility Shift) and conditional procs (Stone Resonance). While Resonance: Attuned Barrier offers moderate support, it doesn't compensate for her inconsistent damage application compared to peers like dedicated damage dealers in S- or A+. Unstable Aegis: Magic Misfire's stun is unreliable, further limiting her disruptive potential. She's outperformed by more consistent damage-focused units, and her hybrid role is executed better by more specialized support characters; a cohesive identity is lacking, causing her kit's synergy to fall flat and contributing to her placement in the overcrowded A-tier.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Vivian's kit revolves around empowering allies and debuffing enemies using the 'Fortuitous Strike' mechanic. 'Mystic's Intuition' feeds into 'Stone Infusion', creating a rewarding gameplay loop where maximizing 'Fortuitous Strike' uptime leads to stronger ultimates.

His effectiveness hinges on cooldown management and understanding which alien form best suits the current scenario.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Ben benefits from allies who can capitalize on his flexible abilities, such as damage amplifiers or those who can enable his transformations through crowd control. He can disrupt enemy formations with Humungousaur's knockback, deal sustained damage with Swampfire's burn, or evade threats to buy time for his team.
character_v1.tierSummary: Ben Tennyson, stuck in C-tier, suffers from diluted jack-of-all-trades syndrome; his kit lacks the focus necessary for impactful performance in any specific role. While "Hero Time" offers burst potential, its reliance on short Omnitrix cooldowns is insufficient to elevate his overall damage output or control capabilities compared to specialized peers. Swampfire's regeneration is negligible, and the reactive shift is inconsistently impactful due to his low base stats. Ultimately, Ben's kit provides no compelling reason to select him over higher-performing characters with clear strengths.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Ben's kit encourages strategic form-swapping, utilizing the Omnitrix Cooldown to maximize the Adaptive Omnitrix Matrix buff. 'Hero Time' allows for rapid transformations and shield generation, complementing his defensive repositioning from Alien Reflexes.

abilities.description: Bruce Wayne, ever the strategist, anticipates his adversary's moves with unnerving precision. Upon activation, for the next 3 seconds, Bruce is primed to evade a single, imminent attack, showcasing his masterful agility. Should an enemy attempt to strike during this window, Bruce executes a seamless dodge, momentarily becoming invulnerable as he vanishes in a swirl of shadows. This evasion allows Bruce to instantaneously reposition himself up to 15 units away, expertly maneuvering towards the enemy backline to disrupt their formation and sow chaos amongst their ranks. This repositioning is carefully delayed by ~10% to give opponents slightly more time to react, ensuring engagements feel deliberate and measured. The successful dodge also grants Bruce 5 stacks of 'Preparedness', each stack increasing his tactical acumen. 'Preparedness' stacks cap at 20, representing the pinnacle of his combat readiness. Even while hampered by crowd control effects, Bruce's sheer force of will allows him to activate Calculated Evasion. character_v1.playstyle: Dandy is a support character that can transition into a bruiser. His abilities focus on buffing allies and manipulating the economy, with the option to transform into a more aggressive Twisted form using Ichor Reserves.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Dandy excels in teams that can consistently secure kills, maximizing the benefits of his signature passive. character_v1.tierSummary: Dandy's S-tier placement is questionable; while his support kit offers a unique blend of utility and resource management with 'Dandy's Bargain' and 'Ichor Dividend,' his direct impact on the fight pales in comparison to peers like Minnie Mouse who offer more consistent and potent buffs. 'Prismatic Bloom' has burst potential, but the high Ichor cost and transformation delay make it unreliable in the current meta dominated by faster, more decisive ultimates. He's essentially a discount enabler in a landscape where raw power and immediate effect reign supreme; requiring too much setup for debatable returns. His reliance on specific ability timings for maximum value, particularly with 'Ichor Dividend' scaling, leaves him vulnerable to disruption and outpaced by simpler, more effective support options.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Dandy's kit revolves around generating and spending Ichor Reserves. His passive and first two abilities help him generate Ichor, while his ultimate consumes it for a powerful transformation. His signature passive further rewards team success, creating a positive feedback loop.

Upon activation, Kyle emits a pulsating wave of temporal energy, momentarily disrupting the flow of combat calculations and affording his allies a significant tactical advantage. This ability doesn't directly heal or deal damage, but instead grants a multi-layered defensive buff. Primarily, it immediately grants a moderate damage mitigation shield to the ally with the lowest current health percentage, scaled to Kyle's defense stat and resistance to temporal manipulation. In addition, all allies receive a temporary, but potent, buff to their resilience against crowd control effects, reducing the duration of stuns, snares, and other debilitating conditions by a considerable margin. Furthermore, during the duration of this effect, allies also gain a minor increase to their action speed, allowing for swifter execution of attacks and abilities. The effect lingers for a short duration, requiring precise timing and tactical awareness to maximize its impact on the battlefield, turning the tide of perilous engagements.

abilities.description: Channeling his desperate knowledge of guerilla warfare, Kyle Reese quickly crafts a devastating pipe bomb, a crude but effective weapon born from the ashes of a ruined future. He expertly hurls this makeshift explosive towards a targeted location, the device arcing through the air like a harbinger of destruction. Upon impact with the ground or reaching the apex of its trajectory, the pipe bomb emits a series of rapid, urgent beeps, signaling its imminent detonation. After a nerve-wracking 1.5-second delay, the pipe bomb erupts in a cataclysmic explosion. The blast inflicts X + (1.1 * atk) physical damage to all enemies caught within a 25-unit radius; 'X' representing the base damage and 'atk' scaling with Reese's attack stat, ensuring relevance throughout a fight. The explosive concussive force not only wounds but also incapacitates, stunning all afflicted foes for 1.75 seconds. While stunned, they are helpless, unable to move, attack, or use any abilities, leaving them exposed to further attacks. Given its 55-second cooldown, strategic placement and timing are crucial to maximize the potential devastation of the Pipe Bomb Takedown, and to ensure the survival of Reese and his squad.

character_v1.playstyle: Kyle Reese is a protective support character who enhances an ally's survivability while disrupting the enemy team. His abilities allow him to quickly move in and out of danger, providing cover fire and tactical advantages to his team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kyle synergizes well with damage dealers who benefit from increased survivability and disruption. He can protect fragile carries while providing them with an atk boost through Guardian Protocol upgrades. His Flashbangs and Pipe Bomb Detonation can set up opportunities for other team members to capitalize on.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kyle Reese's A tier placement is propped up by Guardian Protocol and Tech-Com Evasion Training which patch up team-wide survivability issues. However, his kit lacks cohesive synergy; Pipe Bomb's zone control conflicts with his buffering role, and Flashbang is easily countered, hamstringing his utility. Compared to peers like Sakura Haruno who offer more consistent healing or Frog's superior tanking, Kyle's contribution is often diluted. While his numbers aren't bad, his niche is too muddled, and he needs better ability scaling or a kit rework to climb higher.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kyle's kit revolves around protecting his designated Ward. Suppressive Fire and Flashbang Grenades allow him to control the battlefield, while his ultimate provides a strong burst of damage and crowd control to turn the tide of battle. Tech-Com Evasion Training ensures he can quickly react to threats and reposition to defend his Ward.

This ability has a fixed range, initiating a short-range dash towards the targeted enemy. If the target is within the effective range, they are struck with three rapid blows. Each blow inflicts Fire damage and has a small chance to inflict the 'Burn' status effect, stacking intensity with each successful hit. The final strike possesses increased critical hit chance, representing Itachi's precision. Enemies inflicted with three stacks of Burn status are vulnerable to an additional effect: 'Amaterasu Whispers', increasing subsequent Fire damage dealt to them. Should the initial target evade the strikes, Itachi reappears a short distance away, maintaining a strategic advantage and preserving his position as a mobile assassin. The afterimages themselves do not inflict damage but can serve as brief distractions, potentially drawing enemy fire or delaying reactions. Use this ability to weave in and out of combat, dealing burst damage and controlling the battlefield.

character_v1.playstyle: Itachi excels at quickly eliminating high-priority targets through strategic use of Genjutsu and Mangekyō Sharingan abilities, requiring precise timing and tactical awareness to maximize damage output and control the battlefield. character_v1.teamSynergy: Itachi works well with teams that can provide additional crowd control or damage amplification, allowing him to maximize his burst damage potential. He excels at picking off high-priority targets, making him a valuable asset in team fights and skirmishes. Teammates that can capitalize on the Magic Defense reduction from Tsukuyomi will further enhance his effectiveness.
character_v1.tierSummary: Itachi's A-tier placement is questionable given the current meta; his delayed burst from Amaterasu and Susanoo, while potent, are easily countered, leaving him vulnerable compared to more immediate assassins. The 'Crow Clone/Tsukuyomi' combo is telegraphed and lacks the setup speed required to consistently punish meta threats. Eternal Mangekyō provides marginal scaling that doesn't compensate for his susceptibility to burst damage and control. He occupies an assassin slot oversaturated with faster, safer, and more impactful options; his reliance on specific ability sequencing makes him predictable and ultimately less viable than other A-tier peers such as Puss in Boots, Trunks, Richard, and Kyubey.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Itachi's kit revolves around the synergy between Tsukuyomi and Amaterasu, allowing for high burst damage when combined. Mangekyō Resonance further amplifies his abilities, rewarding skillful ability usage and strategic decision-making. The Crow Clone Technique provides mobility and utility, while Susanoo serves as a powerful offensive and defensive tool.

abilities.description: Jesse, fueled by nervous energy and a touch of desperation, whips up a batch of his signature product, launching a vial of potent, modified crystal meth at a single, targeted enemy. Upon impact, the vial shatters, dealing an initial 60 magic attack damage directly to the target, momentarily stunning them with the sheer chemical force. Following this initial hit, the targeted enemy is afflicted with 'Bad Cook,' a debilitating status effect that lasts for 4 seconds. 'Bad Cook' causes the target to suffer 20 magic attack damage per second, simulating the internal chaos of a botched recipe. But the effects don't stop there; while under the influence of 'Bad Cook,' the target experiences a 20% reduction in all incoming healing, as their body struggles to cope with Jesse's twisted formula. The real potency of 'Yo, Science!' lies in Jesse's own 'Chemistry' skill. If Jesse's 'Chemistry' talent is at 3 or more stacks, indicating a period of focused and productive cooking, the 'Bad Cook' effect intensifies; the targeted enemy suffers an additional 10% damage from all sources for the duration of the burn, representing their vulnerability to Jesse's perfected recipe. Conversely, if Jesse's 'Chemistry' skill falls below 0 stacks, revealing his distraction or ineptitude, the initial burst of damage is reduced by 50%, showcasing the flawed nature of his creation. Rather than suffering from the burning damage, the target instead experiences a twisted form of aid, receiving healing equal to 1% of their maximum health per second while afflicted by 'Bad Cook,' a paradoxical consequence of Jesse's chaotic cooking.

abilities.description: Jesse, with his street smarts and intuitive grasp of volatile situations, instinctively analyzes the ebb and flow of combat, reacting with uncanny precision. Every 15 seconds, Jesse's HUD displays a 'reading' of the current battlefield state, represented by one of three potential outcomes: 'Hot,' 'Cold,' or 'Neutral,' reflecting the temperature of the conflict. By accurately predicting the immediate consequences of each reading, Jesse gains a 'Clarity' stack, symbolizing his heightened awareness and control. A correct assessment grants 1 'Clarity' stack, indicating his growing focus, while an incorrect assessment causes him to lose 1 'Clarity' stack, reflecting his wavering attention. These stacks are persistent yet volatile, embodying Jesse's fluctuating state of mind, and range from -5 to 5. As Jesse levels up, the predictive challenge intensifies, requiring him to adapt and refine his tactics. For each 'Clarity' stack, Jesse gains 1% tenacity and 0.5% evasion, up to a maximum of 5% tenacity and 2.5% evasion when he reaches 5 stacks, underscoring his resilience and agility. Conversely, negative stacks reflect Jesse's growing disorientation, reducing his tenacity and making him more vulnerable to crowd control effects.

character_v1.playstyle: Jesse is designed as a volatile support character whose effectiveness depends on correctly predicting chemical reactions, enabling both support and disruptive builds. His focus leans toward a support role, providing buffs and debuffs that can be enhanced through successful Chemistry stacks.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Jesse synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on the buffs and debuffs he provides, such as attack-damage heavy compositions or burst damage comps. His ultimate enables him to lock in a desired chemical state and augment his support/damage output.
character_v1.tierSummary: Jesse Pinkman's kit suffers from severe anti-synergy, oscillating between weak, redundant fire damage and anemic supportive abilities that fail to meaningfully impact engagements. Compared to other supports, his utility is negligible; 'Yo, Science!' is easily avoided and provides minimal area denial, while 'Blue Sky Blitz' offers unreliable damage and healing. His passive is statistically insignificant, and his ultimate, 'Yeah, Bitch! Chemical Firestorm,' is too slow and telegraphed to reliably land, further cementing his position as a bottom-tier character. The lack of cohesive strategy renders him completely outclassed by peers who provide consistent, reliable support or damage output.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Jesse's kit revolves around the Chemistry mechanic, where positive stacks boost offensive capabilities and shield, and negative stacks boost sustain. The success of his abilities is determined by the players capacity to manipulate Chemistry, rewarding strategic choices.

character_v1.playstyle: Darth Vader excels as a control-oriented tank, using his Force abilities to disrupt enemies, absorb damage, and control the battlefield. His resource management centers around building Hatred stacks to empower his abilities and enhance his resilience, enabling him to withstand significant amounts of damage while maintaining control of the fight.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Darth Vader synergizes well with teams that can capitalize on his disruptive abilities and provide additional survivability. Allies that can provide healing or shields can further enhance Vader's ability to generate Hatred and withstand incoming damage. Damage dealers who benefit from controlled enemies, such as those stunned or pulled by 'Force Choke' and 'I Find Your Lack of Faith Disturbing', can maximize their effectiveness. Additionally, allies that can inflict Crowd Control effects can help Vader generate more Hatred, further amplifying his abilities.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Darth Vader's kit revolves around managing Hatred stacks, which are generated through damage taken, damage dealt, and specific abilities. This creates a cohesive playstyle where Vader must balance aggression with defense, using 'Deflecting Strikes' to absorb damage and generate Hatred, then expending it with 'Force Choke' or 'I Find Your Lack of Faith Disturbing' for amplified effects. 'Boundless Rage' provides a constant source of Hatred, making him more resilient and powerful as he endures enemy attacks. 'Sith Meditation' enhances Vader's Crowd Control resilience, while also bolstering his Hatred generation when subjected to debuffs.

character_v1.playstyle: Luke Skywalker is designed as a damage dealer with significant utility and support capabilities, fitting his role as a Jedi. His abilities balance aggressive lightsaber combat with strategic Force abilities to empower both himself and his team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Luke provides damage and moderate utility to his team. His 'Force Push Barrage' can disrupt enemy formations, and 'Jedi Resilience' enhances his survivability, allowing him to stay in the fight longer and support allies. Luke is also a strong choice as a carry hero.
character_v1.tierSummary: Luke's kit suffers from a disjointed identity, mixing damage and control elements without excelling at either, leaving him outclassed within the damage roster. His damage output is moderate, but lacks the burst or consistency required to compete with higher-tier damage dealers, and his control is unreliable due to limited status duration and susceptibility to tenacity. The Force Potential resource mechanic offers minimal impact, failing to meaningfully enhance Luke's core capabilities in the face of more impactful passives. Jedi Resilience provides negligible survivability, offering only a small shield that is easily broken in the current meta's damage-heavy environment, rendering Luke a suboptimal choice compared to specialized damage characters or more robust controllers.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Luke's abilities are designed to synergize around building and expending Force Attunement. 'Flashing Blade Assault' generates Attunement, while 'Force Push Barrage' expends it for control. His Ultimate consumes all Attunement for a massive burst. The passive provides sustain and baseline generation.

character_v1.playstyle: Han Solo excels as a skirmisher, using his mobility and blaster skills to disrupt enemy formations while supporting allies with well-timed debuffs. His kit encourages aggressive positioning and skillful resource management of Smuggler's Luck stacks to maximize damage and utility.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Han Solo synergizes well with teammates who can apply status effects, increasing the effectiveness of 'Quick Draw Blaster Shot'. He also benefits from allies who can capitalize on the 'Marked' and 'Disrupt' debuffs. He provides a solid mix of sustained damage and utility, making him a versatile addition to most team compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Han Solo's C-tier status is cemented by his kit's lack of cohesive synergy; 'Lucky Shot' is his only reliable damage source, while the rest is diluted utility. Compared to skirmisher peers and the broader roster, his damage output and survivability are subpar, rendering him a liability. The inconsistent 'Never Tell Me The Odds' and unreliable 'Evade and Outmaneuver' fail to compensate for his glaring weaknesses. His theoretical 'DL-44 Barrage' AoE is neutered by targeting limitations, making him a fundamentally flawed character.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Han Solo's kit revolves around building and consuming Smuggler's Luck. 'Quick Draw Blaster Shot' benefits from status effects applied by allies or 'Evade and Outmaneuver,' which then can provide a stack of 'Smuggler's Luck'. 'Never Tell Me The Odds' provides sustain and Smuggler's Luck, fueling his other abilities. Smuggler's Tenacity improves survivability. The 'DL-44 Barrage' Ultimate can be empowered by consuming stacks of Smuggler's Luck.

character_v1.playstyle: Leia is designed as a versatile jack-of-all-trades, shifting between support and damage roles using 'Diplomatic Influence'. Her abilities allow her to buff allies and debuff enemies, positioning her as a tactical battlefield commander.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Leia provides significant team-wide buffs, enhancing attack damage, attack speed, and damage reduction. Her shield and debuff abilities offer targeted support and control, making her a valuable asset in various team compositions. Allies who benefit from attack speed and damage amplification will particularly synergize well with Leia's kit.
character_v1.tierSummary: Leia's kit, while synergistic on paper with its reliance on team-wide buffs and targeted support, suffers from inflated stat dependencies and underperforming scaling relative to current S-tier peers like Android 18. Her 'Hope for the Rebellion' aura provides a marginal attack boost, yet is outclassed by dedicated support characters offering superior, more impactful buffs. 'Rebel Command: Blaster Barrage' demonstrates poor damage output despite its debuffing potential, failing to provide the necessary burst needed for control. Though she's meant to be a jack-of-all-trades, the abilities are subpar, and thus, the 'Galaxy to Fight For' passive lacks proper utility. Leia's viability hinges heavily on substantial stat rebalancing or significant skill modifier improvements.

tips: Prioritize building HP: 'Rebel Tactics: Cover Fire' scales with Leia's max HP, making her primary tanking stat also feed her support role.
Time Diplomatic Influence expenditure: Use 'Rebel Tactics' and 'Rebellion's Resolve' strategically to maximize their benefits (shielding, crit chance, CC immunity).

Manage Rebel Coordination effectively: Debuff high-priority targets with 'Rebel Command: Blaster Barrage' to reduce their armor and magic resistance, especially when you have 50 Rebel Coordination available.
strategyData.overview: Princess Leia is a jack-of-all-trades character that focuses on buffing her allies and debuffing enemies. She relies on Diplomatic Influence and Rebel Coordination to amplify her abilities. Managing these resources effectively is crucial. She can be a strong pick but requires careful planning and execution to maximize her potential, because she cannot take a punch.
strategyData.counterplay: Focus fire on Leia to prevent her from buffing allies and debuffing enemies. CC her to interrupt her ability usage and prevent resource generation. Burst her down with high damage dealers, as she has low base HP and relies on shields for survivability. Abilities that remove shields are also effective.

character_v1.internalSynergy: Leia's kit revolves around managing Diplomatic Influence to enhance her abilities. The passive generation of Influence combined with the ability to gain more when allies are in danger creates a dynamic resource system that encourages both proactive support and reactive plays. The Signature Passive synergizes with her Influence-consuming abilities, providing a burst of evasion and potentially saving herself or an ally from death.

Within this field (15 unit radius), all allies gain 15% increased critical hit chance and a 10% bonus to their healing received, bolstering their offensive and defensive capabilities. Enemies within the field suffer a 10% reduction to their accuracy and a 5% decrease to their speed, hindering their attacks and mobility. At the end of the duration, the field explodes, dealing 15 magic damage to all enemies within it. character_v1.playstyle: Lop excels at controlling the battlefield by alternating between supporting allies with buffs and disrupting enemies with debuffs. Resource management and strategic stance switching are key to maximizing her effectiveness.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Lop thrives in a team composition that benefits from increased survivability and disruption. She pairs exceptionally well with damage-focused allies who can capitalize on the advantages granted by Elders' Vigilance.
character_v1.tierSummary: Lop's kit, theoretically a controller, lacks the hard CC or sustained utility necessary to effectively manipulate the battlefield, relegating her to a glorified, understatted support. Compared to other C-tier controllers, her control options are weaker and less reliable, with Adaptable Anomaly's stance change being too slow to meaningfully impact fights. The synergy between her abilities is minimal; Caravan's Cover provides a weak shield while Elders' Vigilance, her ultimate, offers negligible debuff utility. Ultimately, Lop fails to carve a niche, being outclassed in both support and control by roster peers, rendering her unviable in competitive play.

tips: Abuse the short range of Steadfast Bloom to bait enemies closer to your allies, as she wants to brawl and will be more effective when near others.
Keep Force Potential in mind when using Leap of Tao and Lightsaber Reflection; play around the buffs based on your team comp.

Prioritize supportive actions (shielding, healing, buffing) early on to build Force Potential quickly, and then switch to disruptive actions (slowing, stunning, taunting) to maintain a balanced state.
strategyData.overview: Lop is a controller who wants to play aggressively while also being close to her teammates. Her Force Potential passive makes her kit highly variable, but also predictable. Adapt to each game state and exploit enemy positioning, but ultimately you'll struggle to carry.
strategyData.counterplay: Punish her for diving in without her team. CC her to prevent her from taunting or shielding allies. Kite her to prevent her from getting Force Potential.

character_v1.playstyle: Azula is designed as a controller, leveraging her ability to accumulate Combustion stacks to unleash potent area-of-effect stuns and damage. While the original concept suggested an assassin, her area control and the need to build stacks over time better suits the controller role.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Azula excels in teams that can capitalize on her crowd control. Allies who can quickly follow up on her stuns or benefit from reduced enemy damage output synergize well with her. Characters that can provide additional shields or healing can also help her maintain stacks and survive engagements.
character_v1.tierSummary: Azula's kit, while visually appealing, suffers from fractured synergy, failing to establish her as a top-tier crowd controller. Her 'Dazzling Fire Jet Propulsion' offers mobility but lacks reliable follow-up, and 'Lightning Flick Disruption' struggles to consistently apply its disruptive status. Compared to A-tier controllers like Kevin Levin, Azula's control is less consistent and easily countered, hindering her ability to effectively manage the battlefield. The reliance on 'Controlled Fury' for scaling creates a feast-or-famine scenario, easily shut down by early-game aggression or tenacity stacking. 'Sozin's Comet Enhanced Inferno' provides burst, but its long channel time leaves her vulnerable, making it a situational, rather than defining, ability.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Azula's kit revolves around building Combustion stacks with Dazzling Fire Jet Propulsion and basic attacks, then expending them with Lightning Flick Disruption for burst damage and crowd control. Calculated Cruelty enhances her stats based on the number of stacks, incentivizing aggressive play. Sozin's Comet Enhanced Inferno provides a defensive buff and an area-of-effect burst, while Fear is the Only Reliable Way ensures consistent control.

abilities.description: Toph's mastery of earthbending and her profound connection to the ground grant her unparalleled resilience in battle. Each time Toph sustains damage from any source – be it physical attacks, elemental strikes, or even the smallest pebble underfoot – she attunes herself further to the vibrations around her, gaining a stack of 'Fortitude,' increasing her damage reduction by 3% for 4 seconds. This effect can stack up to 5 times, granting a maximum damage reduction of 15%, significantly reducing incoming damage. Each new stack of 'Fortitude' refreshes the duration of all existing stacks, ensuring a sustained defensive posture when under fire. Furthermore, Toph's inherent connection to the earth provides her with a flat bonus to Tenacity, reducing the duration of incoming debuffs by a fixed amount, as well as a flat bonus to Evasion, increasing her chance to completely avoid incoming attacks. This makes her a formidable presence on the battlefield, capable of weathering even the most relentless assaults. Toph's seismic sense extends her awareness beyond mere sight, transforming adversity into an opportunity to harden her resolve and fortify her defenses.

character_v1.playstyle: Toph excels at controlling the battlefield and providing vision, fitting the utility role perfectly. Her kit manipulates terrain and reveals enemies, offering both defensive and offensive options for her team.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Toph is an excellent utility pick, offering vision control and defensive capabilities. Her Earth Wall can protect vulnerable allies, while her slows and reveals help teammates focus fire on key targets. The damage amplification at high levels supports damage-heavy team comps.
character_v1.tierSummary: Toph's S-tier status stems from exceptional area control and defensive utility, enabled by Seismic Shelter and Earthly Fortitude augmenting survivability. Seismic Sense, despite nerfs, still provides crucial accuracy against stealth, setting her apart from peers like Android 18 in target acquisition. While Resolute Bind offers a burst option, its Wind element is thematically incongruent and strategically questionable. Toph's kit synergy shines in defensive stalemates, yet offensive shortcomings relegate her to a reactive, rather than proactive, role, limiting her true potential within the highly aggressive S-tier meta. Compared to Minnie Mouse, Toph sacrifices raw support power for increased battlefield presence.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Toph's kit revolves around using Seismic Sense for enhanced accuracy and vision, allowing her to disrupt and control enemies effectively. Earth Wall provides cover, while Tremorsense Strike slows down targets, making them easier to hit.

abilities.description: Saiyan Pride Assault embodies Vegeta's unyielding ambition and brutal fighting style. As a passive ability, whenever Vegeta lands a critical hit, he gains a stack of 'Pride,' up to a maximum of 5 stacks. Each stack of Pride increases his ATK by 3% and his Critical Hit Damage by 5%. Upon reaching 5 stacks, Vegeta enters a 'Saiyan Surge' state for 10 seconds. In this state, his attacks gain a 20% chance to inflict 'Bleed,' dealing a percentage of the target's maximum health as physical damage over 5 seconds. Furthermore, while in Saiyan Surge, Vegeta's next active ability cast has its cooldown reduced by 25%. This reflects Vegeta's aggressive desire to relentlessly overpower his foes. The potency of the bleed is directly influenced by Vegeta's ATK and critical hit stats, further incentivizing a damage-focused build. Finally, if Vegeta is critically hit while in Saiyan Surge, he unleashes a defiant Ki blast around him, dealing moderate AoE damage and consuming all Pride stacks. This ability represents Vegeta's raw power, aggressive playstyle, and his unending quest to surpass all others. The visual effect is of Vegeta glowing with a fierce, crackling aura upon entering Saiyan Surge.
abilities.flavorQuote: "I will not be outdone! Witness the power of a Saiyan Prince!"

character_v1.playstyle: Vegeta is a high-damage bruiser who thrives in prolonged combat, building up his Saiyan Pride to unleash increasingly devastating attacks. His kit rewards aggression and skillful resource management, allowing him to dominate the battlefield as his power grows.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Vegeta benefits from teammates who can provide consistent damage amplification or healing. He can also act as a secondary damage dealer, providing sustained pressure while other carries unleash their burst damage.
character_v1.tierSummary: Vegeta's kit suffers from disjointed scaling and inconsistent damage output, relegating him to low-tier status; his 'Saiyan Pride' mechanic is a trap, offering negligible benefits compared to other scaling passives. While 'Final Flash' provides burst AoE, its high-risk, high-cooldown nature is easily punished, rendering it unreliable in the current meta. 'Saiyan Rush' is statistically inferior to peers' multi-hit options, and his single-target damage lacks the necessary punch to threaten higher-tier characters. Fundamentally, Vegeta's design fails to capitalize on his intended damage role, making him a suboptimal choice in nearly every matchup.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Vegeta's kit revolves around the 'Saiyan Pride' mechanic, where dealing and taking damage fuels his abilities. His passive provides sustain and increased damage at low health, while his ultimate acts as a powerful finisher that consumes his accumulated Pride.

For enemies whose strength lies in brute force (highest Attack stat), the 'Horror' debuff manifests, crippling their critical strike chance by 30%. Those relying on resilience (highest Defense stat) are plagued by 'Paranoia,' diminishing their shield effectiveness by a quarter. Swift warriors who rely on agility (highest Speed stat) are paralyzed by 'Panic,' their movement speed decreased by 30%. The Scarecrow's power twists each battle into a horrific mirror of the enemy's worst nightmare.

abilities.description: Scarecrow's presence is unnerving, a constant reminder of mortality. The unnatural resilience of his frame grants him a permanent 20 tenacity, reducing the duration of all incoming crowd control effects by 20%. Furthermore, his jerky, unpredictable movements offer a permanent 10 evasion, increasing his chance to dodge incoming attacks, evading harm more easily. When an enemy champion succumbs to their deepest fears, accumulating 4 stacks of 'Phobia' after being repeatedly subjected to Scarecrow’s terrifying gaze and unsettling abilities, Scarecrow capitalizes on their terror. For the next 5 seconds, Scarecrow's next ability cast benefits from a reduced cooldown, shortened by 2 seconds, allowing him to unleash his dark powers more frequently. Simultaneously, the magic damage output of that next ability is amplified by 15%, intensifying the impact of his nightmarish assaults. During this short window of terror-fueled might, Scarecrow also conjures a protective barrier of condensed nightmares, gaining a shield equal to 5% of his maximum health. This ethereal shield endures for 4 seconds, warding off incoming damage and amplifying his terrifying presence across the battlefield, as he becomes a bastion of fear and control.

character_v1.playstyle: Scarecrow is a tactical buffer who excels at applying debuffs and controlling the battlefield. He weakens enemies with fear toxin and phobia stacks, disrupting their damage output and maneuverability. He provides a strategic advantage by crippling key targets from a safe distance.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Scarecrow excels at weakening high-priority targets, making them easier for damage dealers to eliminate. Allies benefit from the reduced damage output of debuffed enemies, increasing the team's overall survivability. His ultimate provides a wide array of debuffs that set up favorable engagements for the entire team.
character_v1.tierSummary: Scarecrow's S-tier placement hinges on his oppressive Phobia debuff application via Reaper's Breath and Psychotoxic Spike, which, when amplified by Master of Psychological Warfare, cripples opponent tenacity and sustain. Reign of Terror's burst and supportive elements grant him tempo control, enabling allies to capitalize on weakened foes. While potent, his reliance on Phobia stacking makes him vulnerable to tenacity-heavy compositions and superior buffers. Compared to peers like Don-Chan, Scarecrow sacrifices raw damage output for debilitating control, carving a niche as a fear-inducing disruptor rather than a dedicated damage dealer; his unique debuff style is the key differentiator for his viability.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Scarecrow's abilities synergize by stacking 'Phobia' on enemies, increasing the effectiveness of his debuffs and triggering bonus effects. 'Hallucinogenic Gas Cloud' and 'Focused Phobia Injection' apply initial stacks, while 'Master of Psychological Warfare' benefits from these stacks. 'Nightmare Symphony' delivers a potent burst of fear and further debuffs, creating opportunities for 'Unshakable Obsession' to provide enhanced abilities and sustain.

abilities.description: Whenever GIR initiates a Disguise shift, his programming goes haywire, imbuing him with a temporary surge of unpredictable power for 6 seconds. This chaotic energy manifests as one of several possible augmentations, chosen completely at random. He might suddenly find himself with a 15% increase to his Attack damage, making his strikes hit harder and his lasers burn brighter. Or perhaps his Magic Attack will skyrocket by 15%, causing his bizarre gadgets to unleash even more potent effects. He could also become surprisingly resilient, gaining a 10% boost to his Defense, allowing him to withstand more physical punishment, or a 10% increase to his Magic Resistance, shrugging off magical attacks with ease. He may even experience a sudden burst of speed, gaining 20 bonus Speed and allowing him to zip around the battlefield like a hyperactive squirrel. This passive also triggers 'Disguise Roulette', forcing GIR to rapidly cycle through all available Disguises in a haphazard sequence. The erratic nature of this passive reflects GIR's unpredictable behavior, sometimes leading to hilarious and devastating results.

abilities.description: GIR, overwhelmed by the sheer magnitude of his impending DOOM-related tasks, inadvertently unleashes a surge of manic, sparkly energy. This outburst manifests as a single-target buff, automatically targeting the nearest allied combatant in need of immediate assistance. That ally receives a hefty action speed increase for 4 seconds, representing GIR's attempt to make them "do more stuff, faster!" This haste is fueled by GIR's Luck and character level, providing a base bonus plus a scaling factor of 0.15 per level and 0.2 per luck, ensuring continued utility as GIR grows. However, true to GIR's chaotic nature, the recipient experiences a brief defense debuff after the frenzied energy subsides. For 2 seconds after the initial 4 second buff, their armor is reduced by 15%, representing the post-frenzy exhaustion of trying to keep up with GIR's... enthusiasm. Strategic usage is key, as timing the 'Sparkly Doom Frenzy' just before a crucial battle moment can significantly boost an ally's output, although be mindful of the brief vulnerability period immediately afterward.

character_v1.playstyle: GIR's kit is designed around rapidly switching between disguises, each granting unique buffs to allies and debuffs to enemies. This chaotic, supportive playstyle emphasizes strategic timing and positioning to maximize team benefits while disrupting the opposition.
character_v1.teamSynergy: GIR excels in teams that benefit from consistent buffs and disruptive crowd control. His speed boosts, damage buffs, and accuracy debuffs enhance the effectiveness of damage dealers, while his 'Hypnotize' ultimate provides valuable disruption in team fights.
character_v1.internalSynergy: GIR's kit revolves around constant disguise changes, triggered by abilities and enhanced by his passive. This creates a dynamic playstyle where buffs and debuffs are applied rapidly, requiring strategic ability usage and timing to maximize their impact.

abilities.description: Fabulous Phantasmagoria is HIM's signature passive, transforming the battlefield into a surreal nightmare befitting his flamboyant malevolence. Upon activating an ability, HIM doesn't merely strike; he *invites* a single enemy (prioritizing heroes with the lowest magic resistance) to a private showing of their innermost fears. The target is engulfed in a crimson spotlight as a grotesque stage manifests around them, complete with grotesque, giggling marionettes performing an unsettling ballet. These infernal puppets inflict a burst of initial magic damage equal to 40% of HIM’s MAG and then torment the victim with a dark damage-over-time (DoT) effect for 4 seconds. This DoT deals an additional 10% of HIM's MAG per tick. HIM's Critical Hit Chance is directly proportional to the puppet's performance flair, increasing the DoT damage by 5% per 10% crit chance, maxing out at a 25% increase. Similarly, HIM’s Critical Damage buffs the audience reaction – extending the duration of the DoT by 0.5 seconds per 25% crit damage, to a maximum of 2 additional seconds. While afflicted by this spectacle, the victim is vulnerable, suffering a 'Stage Fright' debuff for 2 seconds. This debuff increases the duration of slows and snares applied by HIM or allies by 50% and additionally reduces magic resistance by 15%. The chaos of the Phantasmagoria creates an illusion around HIM as well, granting him a 10% movement speed increase for 3 seconds after the ability activates.

character_v1.playstyle: HIM is a trapper who controls the battlefield by inflicting 'Dissonance' and manipulating enemy positions. His kit is designed to disrupt enemy formations, weaken their defenses, and empower allies by consuming the negativity he generates.
character_v1.teamSynergy: HIM excels in teams that capitalize on debuffs and damage amplification. Allies with high burst damage benefit from the increased damage taken by enemies with 'Dissonance'. Supports that provide additional status effects further enhance HIM's magic attack bonus from 'Omnipresence'.
character_v1.internalSynergy: HIM's kit revolves around applying and consuming 'Dissonance'. 'Sinister Suggestion' and 'Claw Swipe' apply Dissonance, while 'Transformation' enhances Dissonance application and provides a burst of damage and stun. 'Emotional Resonance' amplifies damage and increases tenacity, rewarding coordinated debuffing.

Furthermore, the King's intense cold seeps into the very marrow of his foes, inflicting 80 magical damage plus an additional 30% of Ice King's magic attack as magic damage every single second. character_v1.playstyle: The Ice King is designed as a tank, utilizing ice-based abilities to control the battlefield and protect allies. His abilities create area denial and hinder enemy movement, forcing them to engage on his terms while providing sustain and threat generation.

His ultimate creates this terrain and allows Ice King to take full advantage of his passive and other abilities.

character_v1.playstyle: Mega Man excels as a versatile jack-of-all-trades, leveraging his ability to copy enemy abilities to adapt to diverse combat scenarios. His kit balances damage output with strategic control, allowing him to function effectively in various team compositions and respond dynamically to enemy threats.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Mega Man synergizes well with teams that can apply a variety of status effects, enabling him to maximize his damage output through 'Pacifist's Insight'. He also benefits from allies who can provide shields or healing, allowing him to aggressively utilize the Double Gear system without fear of immediate repercussions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Mega Man's viability hinges on 'Weapon Archive,' a highly variable ability that suffers from inconsistency despite its potential for game-changing utility. While 'Double Gear' offers burst potential, its conditional activation and brief duration limit reliable impact, placing him below consistent A+ damage dealers and controllers. His kit lacks cohesive synergy, with 'Heroic Resolve' being a lackluster passive that doesn't compensate for his mediocre base stats. Relative to A-tier peers, Mega Man offers niche adaptability but struggles to excel in any specific role, making him a suboptimal pick in optimized compositions.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Mega Man's kit revolves around adapting to enemy compositions and exploiting vulnerabilities. 'Weapon Archive' allows him to copy crucial enemy abilities, while 'Pacifist's Insight' rewards tactical targeting of enemies with existing status effects. The 'Double Gear System' provides a powerful burst of damage or utility, while 'Heroic Resolve' ensures survivability and resilience.

chapters.title: Emulating the Elite
chapters.mission: Defeat 3 waves of enemies using abilities copied from the first enemy in each wave.
chapters.summary: Mega Man feels frustrated relying only on copied abilities. He seeks advice from Vilgax, a master of stealing and adapting powers, hoping to refine his approach and truly make copied abilities his own.
chapters.bondRewardHint: Vilgax's Arsenal Schematic

chapters.title: A Spark of Inspiration
chapters.mission: Complete a battle using ONLY Mega Man's default abilities, no copied powers.
chapters.summary: After a particularly rough battle, Mega Man feels discouraged. Roll encourages him to see his unique ability to adapt as a strength, not a weakness, reminding him of the potential for creativity and innovation in his playstyle.
chapters.bondRewardHint: Roll's Support Module

This campaign explores his journey of adaptation, discovering that even a hero dedicated to peace must sometimes embrace the power of battle to protect what he holds dear. He learns to balance his pacifistic ideals with the pragmatic realities of combat, forging strong bonds in the process.

abilities.description: With a mischievous grin, Bart Simpson swiftly tags the ground with a vibrant, semi-visible El Barto sticker. This acts as a devious trap, remaining active for 10 seconds, ready to surprise unsuspecting foes who dare to wander within a 6-unit range of Bart and step onto the sticker. The El Barto tag is almost imperceptible unless an enemy is within a mere 3 units of it, adding to its mischievous effectiveness. Upon triggering, the sticky tag not only inflicts immediate physical damage that scales with Bart's attack stat but also applies a 20% Slow, hindering the enemy's movement for 2 seconds. To add insult to injury, it also applies one stack of the 'El Barto Tag' status effect, marking them as a prime target for Bart's other antics. There's a 1-second arming time before the trap becomes active and a maximum of 2 traps can be present on the field simultaneously, requiring strategic placement.

abilities.description: Unleash El Barto's creative chaos! Bart channels his inner street artist, bombarding a targeted enemy and the immediate surrounding area with a high-velocity barrage of spray paint canisters. Upon activation, Bart pulls out a hidden arsenal of multicolored spray cans, rapidly selecting a primary target. He then proceeds to hurl these paint-filled projectiles with surprising accuracy. Each can explodes on impact, dealing consistent Wind-element damage in a small radius. The paint also applies a stacking debuff called 'Tagged,' which slightly reduces enemy evasion and increases critical hit chance against them by the attacker for a short duration. The power of this attack comes not just from the impact, but from the sheer volume of spray; thus, it scales magnificently with ATK and Luck. Further, the multi-hit nature of this ultimate allows for the chance to proc various on-hit effects, making it an excellent combo starter or finisher. Cowabunga!

character_v1.playstyle: Bart excels at disrupting enemy formations and briefly disabling key targets. His kit focuses on applying 'El Barto Tags' to control the battlefield and punish predictable movements, embodying his chaotic and prankster nature. He is not designed for direct damage dealing but rather for area control.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Bart synergizes well with teammates who can capitalize on crowd-controlled or vulnerable enemies. His 'El Barto Tag' debuff makes enemies easier to target, and his ultimate provides a window for burst damage. He particularly complements damage dealers who benefit from slowed or charmed targets.
character_v1.tierSummary: Bart's viability as an A-Tier trapper is questionable; his kit lacks the hard CC or burst damage necessary to secure kills within his area denial. 'El Barto's Sticky Tag' offers mild zoning, but its impact is minimal compared to peers. 'Seymour Butz' Blitz's slow debuff is unreliable, and his damage output is underwhelming for his role. He is powercrept; characters like Puss in Boots provide significantly more impactful control and utility. 'Underachiever's Aura' provides niche team utility, but the low impact of crit reduction does not justify the opportunity cost.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Bart's kit revolves around applying 'El Barto Tag' stacks to disrupt and control enemies. Prank Call Barrage quickly applies stacks, while Graffiti Trap provides area denial and applies a single stack. The passive buffs Bart as enemies are tagged and the Ultimate leverages stacked tags to prioritize targets.

character_v1.playstyle: Renji is designed as a tank/bruiser, leveraging his control abilities to protect allies and disrupt enemies while maintaining his own survivability. While the user provided 'disruption specialist', the bias here goes towards tank due to tank being explicitly specified.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Renji excels in teams that benefit from area control and sustained damage. His 'Segmented' debuff can set up opportunities for allies to inflict burst damage, while his Unreachable Fang passive can help protect nearby teammates with damage reduction.
character_v1.tierSummary: Renji's C-tier placement stems from a kit struggling to define its tank role effectively; his survivability is unreliable, and damage output lackluster compared to peers like Meilin Lee or Ice King. While *Serpent's Resilience* provides some team support, its limited range and conditional trigger dilute its impact. *Higa Zekkō: Baboon Fang Bite* provides some value in AoE stun and debuff application, but its inconsistent execution hinders consistent control. Ultimately, Renji's viability is contingent on niche team compositions heavily reliant on sustained close-quarters combat, a rare scenario given the current roster composition.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Renji's kit revolves around applying 'Segmented' to amplify his Higa Zekkō's stun duration and enabling bleed. His passive provides increased defense stacking, rewarding aggressive plays near allies and further enhancing his role as a tank.

character_v1.playstyle: Goku thrives on aggressive combat, building Saiyan Power through skillful attacks and strategic transformations to unleash devastating damage. Managing Saiyan Power is key, as transformations provide significant power boosts but also require careful resource management.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Goku benefits from team compositions that provide sustain and enable aggressive play. Allies that can buff his attack speed or provide shields will help him maintain 'Saiyan Power' and maximize his damage output. His mobility and damage make him effective in both single-target and AoE scenarios.
character_v1.tierSummary: Goku's S-tier damage classification is supported by his potent mix of scaling damage and transformation-based stat boosts, but inconsistencies mar his viability. 'Saiyan Power' scaling is too slow, leaving him vulnerable early despite 'Unbreakable Will's' sustain. 'Super Saiyan Transformation' is gated and lacks the burst to compete with top-tier damage dealers like Zoro. 'Afterimage Strike', despite its multi-hit potential, suffers from unreliable targeting compared to peers, hindering its utility as a reliable opener or escape tool. He needs 'Saiyan Power' to be less of a chore.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Goku's kit revolves around generating and spending 'Saiyan Power' to transform into Super Saiyan forms, enhancing his stats and unlocking new abilities. The passive, 'Saiyan Body Adaptation', fuels this transformation loop, while 'Unbreakable Will: Saiyan Tenacity' provides survivability, and Kamehameha Charge interacts with Super Saiyan 3.

character_v1.playstyle: Ike's skirmisher kit is designed around high mobility and unpredictable disruptions. He excels at weaving in and out of combat, applying debuffs to enemies, and buffing allies with random, chaotic effects, embodying his childlike nature.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Ike provides a mix of support and disruption. His punt can reposition allies or disrupt enemies, while Cookie Monster applies various debuffs. His ultimate offers healing and further disruption, making him a valuable asset to any team composition.
character_v1.tierSummary: Ike's skirmisher role is undermined by his unreliable kit; 'Kick the Baby' is highly situational for repositioning allies, and 'Cookie Monster!' is an inconsistent AoE. Compared to C-tier peers and the wider skirmisher population, Ike lacks the focused damage or reliable control to secure engagements. 'Canadian Knight' offers a temporary buff, but the lengthy transformation and short duration are often insufficient to impact fights. The stacking mechanic of 'Childlike Chaos' is too slow and random to provide consistent utility, hindering synergy and overall viability.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Ike's abilities synergize through the 'Childlike Chaos' mechanic, which builds up with each ability use and triggers a random effect. The Kindergarten Genius passive enhances his abilities based on usage patterns, and the Canadian Knight ultimate consumes Chaos stacks for additional power.

character_v1.playstyle: Kyle is a jack-of-all-trades character who can provide support, debuffs, and even some damage. His versatility stems from his ability to adapt to different situations and turn the tide of battle with his 'Moral High Ground' passive.
character_v1.teamSynergy: Kyle works well in teams that require both sustain and control. His debuffs weaken high-attack enemies, while his buffs and shields protect vulnerable allies. His ultimate can shut down key enemy abilities, making him a valuable asset in various team compositions.
character_v1.tierSummary: Kyle's jack-of-all-trades design results in diluted effectiveness; his kit lacks a cohesive synergy, hindering his role. Compared to peers like Sakura Haruno who excel in targeted support or Luffy who offers direct sustained damage, Kyle's unfocused buffs and debuffs yield subpar results. The 'Voice of Reason' + 'Outraged Rebuke' offers reactive tenacity, yet falls short against preemptive strategies prevalent among S and above tiers. 'Ultimate Argument' targeting the highest attack foe is unreliable due to conditional debuff application, further highlighting his inconsistency. Ultimately, Kyle's fragmented toolkit leaves him overshadowed by more specialized A-tier counterparts.
character_v1.internalSynergy: Kyle's kit revolves around supporting allies and debuffing enemies. The Moral High Ground mechanic empowers his abilities, turning a defensive situation into an offensive opportunity. 'Fiery Rebuke' and 'Eloquent Plea' both benefit from Moral High Ground, while 'Ultimate Argument' disrupts key enemy abilities.

abilities.description: Unikitty, overflowing with happiness and raw energy, unleashes a concentrated beam of pure, unadulterated joy upon a single targeted enemy! The strength of the Rainbow Rave Beam grows exponentially with Unikitty's innate attack power, scaling dynamically based on her ATK stat. The sheer exuberance of the beam inflicts the 'Dazzled' status effect upon impact for a full 2.5 seconds, causing the affected enemy to momentarily lose their bearings amidst the colorful onslaught of pure fun. 'Dazzled' enemies are rendered unable to execute attacks or abilities during the status duration due to being completely overwhelmed by the positive energy.

abilities.description: Unikitty channels her boundless positivity, creating an aura of pure, vibrant joy that radiates outwards, empowering allies and momentarily overwhelming enemies! Friendly champions within a 400-unit radius are invigorated by Unikitty's optimism, granting them a 4% damage reduction as they bask in her radiant energy. Furthermore, these allies receive a burst of healing cheer every second, restoring 3% of their missing health, keeping them in the fight longer and stronger. The sheer force of Unikitty's happiness also overwhelms her foes; enemies within the aura find their attack damage reduced by 8%, as their dark hearts struggle to cope with the intense positivity. However, containing such immense joy is not without its cost; Unikitty's latent sadness bubbles to the surface, granting her 10 armor and magic resistance while the aura is active, representing the emotional strain of keeping her inner turmoil at bay.

abilities.description: When Unikitty's optimism falters and her health dips to a perilous 25%, the repressed fury beneath the surface erupts, unleashing Ultrakatty! For 15 glorious seconds, Unikitty transforms, growing in size and power. In this state, she gains a substantial 50% increase to both her Armor and Magic Resistance, making her a formidable bulwark against incoming attacks. Furthermore, each of Ultrakatty's basic attacks becomes infused with her burning rage, dealing a bonus burst of magic damage equivalent to 10% of her maximum health to her primary target and all nearby enemies within a 250 unit radius. This transformation generates a permanent state of raw, untamed 'Angry' emotion for the duration, amplifying her destructive potential. However, such intense fury cannot be sustained indefinitely. Once the 15 seconds elapse, Unikitty reverts, momentarily exhausted. For 5 seconds after the transformation, her movement speed is reduced by 20%, leaving her vulnerable as she recovers her composure.
